newsitem.title: USA: CSCE May world sugar ends up, funds steady buyers.
newsitem.headline: CSCE May world sugar ends up, funds steady buyers.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled firmer amid steady fund buying that carried May to a six-month high, dealers said.

The contract rose to 11.38 cents, the high made on September 13, before easing back to 11.37 on the close, up 0.06. Second-position July finished 0.11 firmer at 11.17 cents, while the outer months gained 0.07 on the day.
Volume was estimated at 38,723 lots compared with Wednesday's official 55,360 lots.
Producer selling limited gains to below 11.20 cents basis July, where traders cited buy stops.
Today's gains surprised many analysts who expected prices to begin easing towards 11.00 cents ahead of the May options expiry on Friday, since open interest in the May 11.00 calls remains high.
The flurry of speculative buying in July and the persistent buying of the May/July spread overshadowed options expiry, however.
Open interest rose 5,919 lots to 66,980 lots in May and 6,878 lots to 48,959 lots in July, reflecting a surge of new speculative long positions, traders said.
At the same time, speculators have begun rolling May positions into July, and dealers expect the rolling to accelerate after Friday's options expire.
Technically, the market is reaching an overbought condition, "but it's hard to argue that it will go down when the specs have been adding more positions," a trader said.
In fundamental news, Brazil's 1996/97 sugar consumption is expected to reach 8.6 million tonnes, the senior analyst for tropical commodities at Sparks Companies Inc, said.
Peter Buzzanell told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweeteners' Conference in Cancun, that demand could climb to 9.4 million tonnes between 2001-2002.
Mexico's sugar consumption, however, could fall 6 percent to 4.1 million tonnes raw value, this season, Sparks siad.
